messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: soft K-means clustering in Stan
parts:
I wrote up the section for the manual on soft K-means,
and put the relevant pages up on our downloads page:

http://stan.googlecode.com/files/stan-reference-clustering.pdf

Please pay particular attention to the problems for Bayesian
inference posed by clustering section (a toxic combination of
non-identifiability and multimodality).

You can also find the model, an R program to generate
simulated data and an example of simulated data, in
our repository. You can get the relevant files for
soft-k-means here:

http://code.google.com/p/stan/source/browse/#git%2Fsrc%2Fmodels%2Fmisc%2Fcluster%2Fsoft-k-means

I'll add LDA next, but please please read the problems section
before you decide using MCMC for clustering is the way you
want to go.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: soft K-means clustering in Stan
parts:
The means currently form a matrix.

We could definitely do something like define
a kind of lexicographic order on the parameters
and sort them.

Or we could try to add in some kind of asymmetric
prior that would introduce separation. In fact,
maybe we could define some neat new priors thinking
about the problem.

I was going to add some examples with predictive
inference for document similarity or word similarity,
which might be pretty well identified even in the face
of the posterior multimodality.

I didn't want to get too carried away, though.

- Bob
